### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a8358581aab41981c94a697da4d2ef87faca42ac`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **19** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a8358581aab41981c94a697da4d2ef87faca42ac` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e766342cd3ef1bfde65b2caf6cda73aa9b0aaeb1` — the merge of head `80315628e91fdcd3194b61d9489d3f4296be6143` into base `a8358581aab41981c94a697da4d2ef87faca42ac`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e766342cd3ef1bfde65b2caf6cda73aa9b0aaeb1 && git checkout e766342cd3ef1bfde65b2caf6cda73aa9b0aaeb1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a8358581aab41981c94a697da4d2ef87faca42ac 80315628e91fdcd3194b61d9489d3f4296be6143 && git checkout -B drift-repro a8358581aab41981c94a697da4d2ef87faca42ac && git merge --no-ff 80315628e91fdcd3194b61d9489d3f4296be6143

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a8358581aab41981c94a697da4d2ef87faca42ac
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a8358581aab41981c94a697da4d2ef87faca42ac` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `80315628e91fdcd3194b61d9489d3f4296be6143`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/last-admin-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/single-reslug-default-anchor.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/default-organization-statements.golden.test.ts + .changeset/25271-single-reslug-default-anchor.md, packages/core/src/security/default-organization.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/identity-write-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/tenancy-service.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/default-organization-invariant.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-plan.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts, packages/types/src/env.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-organization.object.ts, docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md, docs/adr/0135-identity-and-access-architecture.md, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs

Reviewed at the head the seat named after the merge of `origin/main` (merge commit `e47a5a97e2`, merge base `a8358581aa` = `origin/main`). The three code blobs are byte-identical to `ec6d235613`; only the changeset moved (two bullets and the operator paragraph). Net diff: 4 files, +410 / -8; 0 of 4 paths governed; same-repo head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The narrowing itself — RIGHT.** `guardOrganizationDefaultSlug` (`sys_organization` `beforeUpdate`, priority 20) refuses a payload with `slug = 'default'` unless the addressed set is exactly the current Default Organization, named through `findDefaultOrganization` in `packages/core/src/security/default-organization.ts` (slug `default`, else the sole organization) over a system read. That is the one definition the authorization resolver anchors by (`readDefaultOrganizationId`, `grantAnchorsPlatformStanding`), so the write the hook refuses is exactly the write that would move the `admin_full_access` anchor onto another organization (ADR-0131 D5). The wall short-circuit reads `postureEnforcesWall(resolveTenancyPosture())`, the same read the resolver makes at `resolve-authz-context.ts` (line 1624) and the insert half makes: "no grant anchors under a wall" and "the hook reads nothing under a wall" are one fact. Refusing `isSystem` writes too is correct for a capture guard: the capture doors are the system ones (better-auth's adapter, seeds, plugins).

2. **Door inventory ("every door that can change a slug is an engine update") — RIGHT, verified.** better-auth's adapter writes through the engine (pinned at HTTP: 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, slug unchanged, standing unchanged). The data API's user-context PATCH and update-mode import are closed one layer earlier by the ADR-0092 identity write guard (`identity-write-guard.ts`: `slug` is not in `MANAGED_EXTENSION_EDITABLE_FIELDS.sys_organization`, a non-whitelisted key is stripped, a payload that strips to nothing is refused 403). `updateById` delegates to `engine.update`. The boot invariant (`default-organization-invariant.ts`) only inserts. The ownership ceremony (`organization-ownership-plan.ts`) reads the Default Organization by the same rule and writes no slug. `beforeUpdateOrganization` in `auth-manager.ts` is untouched and still judges only the environment-binding slug lock; the first commit's pre-check and its export were removed, so the engine hook is the single owner of the rule (route and surface ownership, rule 1) and `check:api-surface` sees no export change.

3. **Predicate shapes — RIGHT.** A scoped `multi: true` write fans `beforeUpdate` out per matched row with the batch `options` carried, and `resolveTargetIds` rescans the predicate, so the whole matched set is judged (pinned by predicate). An unscoped `multi: true` write dispatches the whole-operation call only to hooks declaring `dispatchUnscopedMultiWrite` (this one does not), but the per-row fan-out still reaches every registered `beforeUpdate` hook for every matched row, and `resolveTargetIds` then scans the table under `maxScan`: a set of two or more is refused before the unique index. An empty matched set is admitted, correctly (nothing is written). A scan over `maxScan` is a refusal and is re-thrown unchanged.

4. **Fail-closed and the carrier — RIGHT for this card, one asymmetry noted.** The refusal is `PERMISSION_DENIED` + 403, the code every half of this guard answers and `mapDataError` maps (ADR-0112). A read fault (the addressed rows or the Default Organization unreadable) also answers 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, with text that says the read failed and to retry: that is this file's `failClosed` shape, and the changeset discloses it ("a read the guard cannot complete refuses as well"). It is asymmetric with the sibling slug guard in `auth-manager.ts`, whose read fault answers 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` (`slugGuardReadFaultApiError`); the dev measured the move (ablation A1, 503 to 403) and chose the guard's shape. Changing the fault carrier for one half alone would split the invariant's vocabulary, and a dedicated code is a `packages/spec` ledger row outside this card's surface. Noted, not blocking.

5. **Controls — RIGHT.** The sole organization taking `default` is admitted (it already is the Default Organization; its grant already anchors: `platform_admin` true before and after). A slug other than `default` costs no read. Under `isolated` (HTTP) and `group` (engine) the same write is admitted. A `default`-slugged Default Organization beside the target: refused by this rule before the unique index (at HTTP, better-auth's own slug-taken 400 answers first, as the test notes).

6. **Stranding, the derived consequence — RIGHT and now documented.** On a `single` store holding several organizations and none slugged `default`, every re-slug to `default` is a capture and is refused, the previous holder included. That shape is already the tenancy census's `SINGLE_POSTURE_MANY_ORGANIZATIONS` error-level misconfiguration (`tenancy-service.ts`), and the refusal's remedies are the census's two ways out (declare a walled posture, or hold one organization). Moving the Default Organization AWAY while others exist stays with the update half (ADR-0135 D5.2, unchanged): no ADR decision is reversed (Prime Directive 13), and the changeset at this head names both the removed two-step move and the stranding.

7. **Tests — RIGHT.** Ten pins on the real stack (ObjectQL over driver-sql and better-sqlite3, the real guard, a real `AuthManager` with the organization plugin, the real `resolveAuthzContext`), each refusal with its control. The `find` spy narrows the injected fault to this rule's own read (`slug: default`, `limit 1`), so the read-fault pins prove this hook refuses and not the update half; the dev's second A2 run is what forced that narrowing. The runtime golden test previously performed the capture in system context and asserted the standing flip, i.e. it pinned the behaviour this card removes; it is rewritten along the legal path and asserts the refusal (403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`), the memo retirement on withdraw (standing false) and on re-sole (standing true). The exact `organizationReads: 1` count on the withdraw leg was dropped rather than corrected: with no `default` slug the resolver reads twice (by slug, then the count), so a `2` could have been pinned. Weaker, not wrong; non-blocking.

8. **Not a surface change elsewhere.** No export added or removed in the net diff; no `packages/spec` change; no docs claim the removed behaviour (grep over `content/docs`, `docs/`, `skills/` for re-slug and moving the Default Organization: none); no ADR anchor JSON is pinned on `last-admin-guard.ts`; the registration log line is extended truthfully. Not a startup-registry verdict and not a logged degradation: the failure is handed to the caller.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/25271-single-reslug-default-anchor.md` at this head: `'@objectstack/plugin-auth': patch`, a `fix(plugin-auth)!:` summary, the `**BREAKING**` banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its why. Judged:

- **What the diff publishes:** a runtime accept-set narrowing in `@objectstack/plugin-auth` only. The `packages/runtime` change is a test file; no runtime changeset is owed. Correct.
- **Direction and `Clause-②`:** the PR body and the changeset both carry `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`; the change widens no published payload and narrows a write. Both lines match the diff.
- **ADR-0087 disposition:** no key of any metadata schema is removed, renamed or re-shaped, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite and no tombstone is owed; `no-migration-prescription` is the honest category. The body's FROM and TO text is inline prose with no arrow, no vertical FROM and TO pair, no rewrite table and no migration heading, so it carries none of the prescription shapes the gate reads. The `Check Changeset` job, which runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base`, concluded success on this head, so the changeset revision at `80315628e9` has been judged by both.
- **Level:** under the house rule (`Metadata-protocol: none`, with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker, makes `patch` correct for a narrowing), `patch` is correct. The job's conclusion is the verdict of record; nothing was re-derived locally.
- **Migration text:** FROM and TO stated; the operator remedy stated (keep another slug; move the grant, not the slug; hold one organization or declare a walled posture, as the census prescribes). The two bullets added at this head (the removed two-step move; the stranding) are accurate to the code: the update half still admits moving away, the second write is refused.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `premise_still_valid: true` — agreed. `origin/main` at `a8358581aa` still holds the shape; main's side of the merge touched `auth-manager.ts` and `auth-manager-actor-guards.ts` but no file of this PR and not the organization update hook.
- deviation 1, file surface grew by `packages/runtime/src/default-organization-statements.golden.test.ts` — accepted. The fixture pinned the removed capture, went red in Test Core 6/6 at `7aeec2d3`, and is rewritten along the legal path asserting the refusal (judgment ① 7). Within the card; no scope expansion (Prime Directive 10).
- deviation 2, worktree in the cloud container — accepted; process only.
- deviation 3, model-free trailer pair — accepted; it is the AGENTS.md form.
- open question (collateral of the narrow rule), options A / B / C — **answered: A.** The acceptance is "no slug change makes a non-Default organization the Default Organization", and A closes every door with the least collateral. The stranded shape (several organizations, none `default`, under `single`) is the census's error-level undeclared posture with two stated ways out, which the refusal repeats; the changeset at this head documents it. B changes the update half's ADR-0135 D5.2 semantics (refusing a write that leaves an administrator standing) and the claim excluded widening into that territory; C is unsound, since a grant can be written after the slug. If the epic wants the stuck shape unreachable, that is a card of its own, not a condition of this PR.
- out-of-scope finding 1, the `PERMISSION_DENIED` carrier — accepted (judgment ① 4); a dedicated code is a `packages/spec` error-code ledger row outside this surface.
- out-of-scope finding 2, ADR-0131 D5's 2026-10-22 note names the insert half and not this update-side rule — accepted; `docs/adr/**` is excluded by the claim, the ADR id is left in the code, and the epic amends.
- Gate state on this head: 21 check-runs completed (`Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check PR Size`, the claim checks, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Auto Label`, `filter`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`: success; 7 opt-in or full-battery runs skipped), 17 still in progress (`Test Core` 1 to 6, `Build Core`, the remaining `Lint` lanes, the `Type Check` lanes). The code blobs are identical to `ec6d235613`, where the dev reports 34 success / 7 skipped / 0 failed with Test Core 6/6 fixed. **The seat confirms the 17 before posting: this PASS is read with the five required contexts concluding success on `80315628e91fdcd3194b61d9489d3f4296be6143`.**
- Not measured here (read-only): the wall time of the new ten-case suite, which boots a real `AuthManager` per case; if a run shows it over the lane's 10 s rule, that is the lane's card, not this review's.

## Seat check

- **Shape:** 4 files, +410 / −8: `plugin-auth`'s last-administrator guard, its new pin suite, the runtime memo-retirement golden, and one changeset. `check-governed-merges --pr 25286`: not governed, so this is an ordinary queue landing. It touches no ceremony, plan, harness or engine tenancy code, so no `needs:upgrade-harness`.
- **Review tier:** the PR declares `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, so the review is at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the narrowing face. Record 6352123147 on this head: **PASS**, with no item escalated.
- **What it does** (ADR-0131 D5): under `single`, a `sys_organization` slug changed to `default` is admitted only on the organization that already is the Default Organization. Anything else is refused 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` at the engine's `beforeUpdate`, for every context, `isSystem` included. That covers better-auth's `organization/update`, seeds and plugins alike; the data API was already closed by the ADR-0092 identity write guard. Walled postures read nothing and admit; a failed read refuses.
- **The golden rewrite** (`default-organization-statements.golden.test.ts`) is a declared contract change to that case's expectation, accepted. The old case performed the capture this card closes, in system context. The new one keeps the memo-retirement intent in both directions (move off withdraws standing; back to the sole organization confers it) and asserts the capture refused.
- **Open question (stranding), answered A, the dev's and the reviewer's recommendation.** The PR removes one operation, with no in-place replacement: on a `single` store holding several organizations, making a different organization the Default Organization. After `default` is re-slugged away (still admitted by the update half, ADR-0135 D5.2, when an administrator stays standing), no organization can take it back. The seat judged this within the card, with no decision card, because the shape exists only where main already refuses to guess:
  - core `system-write-organization.ts` classifies `single` with several organizations as `ambiguous-organization`;
  - the tenancy census reports it at error level (`SINGLE_POSTURE_MANY_ORGANIZATIONS`);
  - both ways out are stated in the refusal and the changeset: hold one organization, or declare a wall. To move the anchor, move the grant, not the slug.
  - Making the stuck shape unreachable (option B) would change the update half's semantics and is a card of its own if the epic wants it.
- **Carried, not blocking:**
  - a read fault answers 403 here and 503 in `auth-manager`'s sibling slug guard (the guard's `failClosed` shape; a dedicated code needs a spec ledger row);
  - ADR-0131 D5's 2026-10-22 note names the insert half but not this update-side rule. That is for the epic's next ADR amendment, recorded on the #15212 ledger.
- **CI on the head:** 41 check-runs, every one success or skipped (`Test Core` 1 to 6/6, `Build Core`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`); mergeable clean. `main` is merged in with a merge commit (`e47a5a97e2`).
- **R1–R4,** measured by the dev: all on this head, after the main merge.
  - R1: a production `os serve` under `single` on a fresh store answered health, sign-up, sign-in and session 200. The sole Default Organization re-slugs both ways, 200.
  - R4: the same under `isolated` and under `group`, all 200. Two `organization/create` succeed in each, and there are 0 organization-less grants.
  - R2 and R3: the upgrade harness passed 16/16, both fixture legs. The dogfood battery passed 289 files and 2491 tests, 0 failed.
  - Gates: 68 of 69 exit 0. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` was NOT MEASURED (it needs a full build), and CI `Build Core` is green. The PR changes no build or export surface.
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/plugin-auth` `patch`, `fix(plugin-auth)!`, `**BREAKING**`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Right under the house rule; `Check Changeset` is success on this head. The changeset names the removed move and the stranding.
- **Landing:** the seat flips the PR ready and enables auto-merge. `Fixes #25271` closes the card.
